latest.confidence_why: Same-day direction after a 5% headline gap is close to a coin flip: the driver is a sentiment call with pushback already visible (Trump, Burry), the pre-market print has no volume, and the record shows semis is this adviser's weakest cluster (40% hit).
tells: SOXX reclaims the 07:44 ET pre-market print (~501) inside the first hour on rising volume, NVDA green -> semis and ai_power_infra flip to firm (headline dip being bought).
META and GOOG give up their pre-market gains at the open -> rotation story fails, it is outright de-risking; big_tech flips to soft.
10Y trades through 5.00% during the session -> market soft hardens and big_tech goes soft with it.
Explicit White House/Trump action against the slowdown call (beyond Sunday's remarks) -> chips bounce, semis flips to firm.

semis.why: AI-slowdown call (Amodei Sat, Altman/Musk backing) gapped chips -5% pre with no volume behind Friday's 0.75x-volume rally; Asia/Europe confirmed in real volume (hynix -6.6% on 1.26x, Soitec -13.6%, Aixtron -10.3%, Infineon -7.6% regular); hike Wed near-fully priced, 10Y 4.975%, WTI $103 deny the dip-buy. Memory, equipment and the GPU clouds hit hardest; chipmakers proper (NVDA -2.5, AVGO/TSM -3.3) least.

ai_power_infra.why: Bloom -7% pre from +22% above its 50-day = extension unwinding; Infineon/Aixtron already -8/-10% in the European regular session; same SOXX benchmark, same thin US pre-market gap into a hostile macro.

big_tech.why: QQQ -1.4% pre but the platforms are bid against the chips (META +2.7, GOOG +1.5 pre, thin; Reuters snapshot also had both green) - money rotating inside tech, not leaving it (HY flat, VIX/VIX3M 0.94 contango). NVDA/AVGO/AMD drag vs META/GOOG lift nets to QQQ near its pre-market level.

market.why: SPY -0.57% pre has only priced the AI headline; the Fed hike Wed, 10Y just under 5% and oil $103 (Hormuz) build through the session and energy does not offset a tech de-risk. Mild, not sharp: credit and the vol term structure are calm.

sg_banks.why: STI closed +0.36% today against the global risk-off, UOB +2.8% on 1.72x volume (no headline found); banks are rate beneficiaries with the 10Y near 5%, US tech weakness dents the STI only modestly. Next close Tue 17:00 SGT, within the band.

summary.bottom_line: Don't add to chips or AI-power names today, and don't buy the dip before Wednesday's Fed decision. Hold the platform names. Expect the chip selloff to extend into the close rather than fill.

summary.macro_attribution: Since Friday's close the biggest movers are oil (WTI +2.7% to $103 on the Hormuz standoff) and the VIX (+10% to 17.5); the 10-year is up 3bp at 4.975%, the dollar +0.4%. Today's leans rest on the AI headline, not on oil. The 10-year near 5% and the hike are why I don't expect a dip-buy to hold.
what_happened: Anthropic's Amodei called Saturday for slowing frontier AI development; Altman and Musk backed him, and OpenAI shelved its IPO (CNBC Sep 12, Reuters via Investing.com Sep 14 05:16 ET). Trump pushed back Sunday (NPR Sep 13). This is a sentiment shock to AI-capex durability, not a demand data point.
Asia and Europe confirmed it in real volume: SK hynix -6.6% on 1.26x average volume, Samsung -4.1%, KOSPI -3.3%, Soitec -13.6%, Aixtron -10.3%, Infineon -7.6%, all in regular sessions (tape).

US chips gap -5% pre-market with no volume behind it (tape). Friday's +5% five-day run was on 0.75x volume, so there is no committed buyer base under it. Memory (Micron -5.5%, Sandisk -6%), equipment (ASML -5.7%) and the GPU landlords CoreWeave and Nebius (-7.6%, -8%) are hit hardest; chipmakers proper least (Nvidia -2.5%, Broadcom and TSMC -3.3%).

The platforms are bid against the chips: Meta +2.7%, Google +1.5% pre-market (tape; a Reuters snapshot also had both green, one Investing.com snapshot had both red, so thin and flagged). Credit is flat and the VIX curve is still calm, so this reads as rotation inside tech, not an exit.
Bloom Energy, a fuel-cell company, is -7% from 22% above its 50-day: an extension unwinding, not a fundamental break (tape).

change_my_mind: SOXX reclaims its pre-market print in the first hour on rising volume with Nvidia green: chips flip to up.
Meta and Google give up their gains at the open: rotation story fails, big tech flips to down.
The 10-year trades through 5.00%: market and big tech both go down.
Explicit White House action against the slowdown call: chips bounce.
summary.confidence: Same-day direction after a 5% headline gap is close to a coin flip, and semis is this adviser's weakest cluster.
summary.cant_know: Whether dip-buyers show up at the open before the Fed, and whether the pre-market platform bid is real.
summary.the_call: Down, moderately. Chips off another 0.5 to 1.5% from the pre-market level, with memory, equipment and the GPU clouds taking the worst of it and the chipmakers proper holding up better. The whole market drifts mildly lower, and the platforms (Meta, Google) move least.
